notes: The attached booklet had only the cover page and a promotional page for other Friends sets. It showed no building steps. The sub-assemblies, their order and the rests_on relations are my own plausible guesses, not read from the manual.

The remaining 'many separate groups' warning is not a real problem for this set. Set 3316 is a 24-door advent calendar. Each door holds a small separate mini-build or a few loose accessories, and the booklet builds separate small models, not one big model.

I did not join the groups together. The booklet showed no step that links them, and many pieces (hair accessories, skis, poles, starfish, bone, wand, gem, carrot tops) have no studs or clutch ports. Adding links would invent connections the set does not have.
The dog (b74) stands loose on the round tile, which has no studs, so its rests_on is empty and the placement is recorded as an other_join.
The parts list is the only reliable source: all 206 pieces appear once (b1 to b206) and the count of every type and colour matches it.
The 16 hair-accessory pins and 4 bar accessories are loose pieces. Only two example pin joins to the hair piece are recorded.
Some bases hold more pieces than their studs would allow (for example the 4x4 round plate under the tree). These are placement guesses.
Position is null for every piece.

graph_initial.title: LEGO Friends Advent Calendar 2012 (3316-1)

edges.freedom: removable; any hair accessory pin can be placed in the hair hole

edges.method: broom handle held in horizontal clip
carrot top bar pushed into stud
carrot top bar pushed into stud
leaves bar held in bar-up piece

notes: The attached booklet only contained the cover page and a promotional page for other Friends sets. It showed no building steps, so the sub-assemblies, their order and the rests_on relations are my own reasonable guesses and not read from the manual.
What I could rely on: the parts list. All 206 pieces are listed once, b1 to b206, and the count of every type and colour matches it (I summed the 100 lines to 206).

The grouping follows the 24-day calendar idea: doll head with hair, hair accessories, skis and poles, lodge, post, tea set, cupcakes, flower garden, dog park, fence, snowman, tree, plane, box, pink room, yellow plane, plant pot, bucket and bag, ice rink, lights, and so on.
The 16 hair-accessory pins (bows, butterflies, flowers, hearts, stars, glasses, crown) and the 4 bar accessories are loose pieces. Only two pin joins to the hair piece are recorded as examples.
Parts with no connection ports (starfish, gem, skis, poles, bone and similar) are loose or simply resting. Where I could not tell what they sat on, rests_on is empty or a guess.
The 4x4 round plate and similar bases hold more pieces than their studs would allow in a few places. These are placement guesses.
Position is null for every piece.

final_issue_list: the build is 60 separate groups of pieces; connect them unless the booklet really builds separate models
